title: Controls that make a DREADD study rigorous
objective: List the control groups a DREADD experiment needs and say which confound each one rules out.

steps.title: Every DREADD result has two suspects
steps.body: When your [[DREADD]] animals change after you give the [[actuator]], two things could be responsible: **your neurons** (what you want) or **the actuator itself** (the confound from L3). Good controls separate them. Think in terms of 'DREADD present/absent' × 'actuator present/absent'.

visual.alt: A 2x2 grid; when the actuator is applied, only the DREADD-positive, actuator-positive quadrant responds while the three controls stay silent, making the result interpretable.
visual.caption: Only the DREADD+ / actuator+ quadrant responds — the rest stay silent.

steps.title: The core groups
steps.body:
A clean design usually includes:

1. **DREADD+ / actuator** — the experimental group.
2. **DREADD+ / vehicle** — tests for leaky or constitutive DREADD activity without drug.
3. **DREADD− / actuator** — tests the actuator's own effects (the L3 confound).
4. **Reporter-only or non-DREADD virus** — controls for surgery/virus/expression, not just the drug.

visual.alt: Interactive control grid: toggle DREADD and actuator on/off, and an actuator off-target switch, to see which quadrant is interpretable.
visual.caption: Flip the switches — see which result is actually interpretable.

steps.prompt: Match each control to what it rules out.
pairs: Leaky or constitutive DREADD effect without drug
Off-target effects of the actuator itself
Effects of surgery, virus, or expression per se
steps.explanation: Each control isolates one alternative explanation. Missing one leaves that explanation open.

steps.prompt: You see an effect in DREADD+ / actuator AND the same-sized effect in DREADD− / actuator. What's the correct conclusion?
options: Your neurons must have driven the observed effect
The effect is the actuator's, not your neurons' own
The DREADD must be unusually strong in these mice
You just need more animals to reveal the difference
steps.explanation: If the DREADD-free group shows the same change, the actuator alone explains it. Your neuronal manipulation added nothing detectable on top.

variants.setup: You see an effect in DREADD+ / actuator — but the same-sized effect in DREADD− / actuator.
options: Your neurons must have driven the observed effect
The effect is the actuator's, not your neurons' own
The DREADD must be unusually strong in these mice
You just need more animals to reveal the difference
variants.reveal: An equal effect without the DREADD means the actuator, not your neurons, is responsible.

steps.title: Don't forget the manipulation check
steps.body: Controls tell you the effect is real; a **manipulation check** tells you the DREADD actually did its job. For activation ([[hM3Dq]]): [[c-Fos]], or ex vivo recording showing increased firing. For silencing ([[hM4Di]]): recording/calcium imaging showing reduced responses. Without this, a null result is uninterpretable — maybe the neurons were never affected.

steps.scenario: Your hM4Di pancreas experiment shows NO change in the readout after the actuator. Reviewers ask whether the silencing even worked.
options: A clear photograph of the mice taken before and after
Imaging or recording showing the DREADD+ neurons were suppressed
The genotyping PCR that confirms the DREADD allele is present
A longer video recording of the behavioral session
steps.explanation: A null result only means something if you can show the manipulation worked. Direct evidence that the neurons were silenced turns 'it didn't work' into 'silencing these neurons has no effect on this readout' — a real finding.
steps.followUp: Also check expression ([[reporter]]) in the right cells and the actuator dose/timing.
